name: backlog_lanes
about: Default panel rubric, criteria ids and scales set by the scoring redesign (lanes). Each judge scores one candidate blind. The panel writes medians, spreads and disagreement; `python -m lab.tools.backlog panel` turns them into lanes. Gates are probabilities a judge assigns, not kills: the lane logic decides what a gate does.

criteria.question: Probability that a known theorem, a published result or one of the lab's own verdicts already rules this claim out. Name it in strongest_objection if above 0.3.
Probability that the result is a step toward an algorithm the lab itself owns (1), rather than only refuting or reproducing other people's work (0).

Highest result rung reached if the claim holds: 1 sharp negative / dequantization, 2 quantum-inspired classical method, 3 measured mechanism, 4 small-scale separation on quantum-native data, 5 crossover resource estimate, 6 advantage on real data and hardware.
Probability that the claim holds at its own operating point when tested (not the probability that it is publishable).

If it works, what does the lab own? 1 nothing: it refutes or reproduces other people's work; 2 a measured property, baseline or tool the lab's own method needs; 3 a working small-scale version of the lab's own method, or its cheapest fatal check passed; 4 the lab's method beats a strong classical baseline in a named regime; 5 an advantage on a path to real data or hardware. Ignore plausibility here.
0 no reason beyond 'try it'; 1 a vague reason; 2 a named, non-consensus reason why it should work that most of the field would not already assume. Put the reason in strongest_case.
Cost in days of agent and simulator time of the cheapest experiment that could kill this claim.
1 if you would spend a week of the team's time on this now, else 0. Be selective: across a whole backlog you may champion at most 3 candidates.
